title: Counting the Time a Piece Has Been at the Bench
content:
# Desk Standing Rule: Counting the Time a Piece Has Been at the Bench

Where the time a piece has been at the bench of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service bears on a work order, the day that time is counted from turns on two records on that order: whether a check that found rework needed stands on it, and whether any amount has already been taken off it.

## 1. A check that found rework needed, with amounts already taken off

Where a check that found rework needed stands on the work order and amounts have already been taken off it, the time at the bench is counted from the day of the most recent such check.

## 2. A check that found rework needed, with nothing taken off

Where such a check stands on the work order and no amount has been taken off it, the time at the bench is counted from the day the customer authorised the work.

## 3. Any other case

In any other case the day the time is counted from is not moved on these grounds.

## Anchor table

| A check that found rework needed stands on the order | Amounts already taken off the order | The day the time at the bench is counted from |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the day of the most recent such check |
| yes | no | the day the customer authorised the work |
| no | yes | not moved on these grounds |
| no | no | not moved on these grounds |

## A hypothetical reading

A work order shows the piece taken in on the 2nd of a month, the work authorised on the 6th, two checks that found rework needed logged on the 11th and the 19th, and 40.00 USD taken off the order. The day the time at the bench is counted from is the 19th, the most recent of the two checks. Had nothing been taken off that order, it would have been the 6th, the day the customer authorised the work.
